papers.version_note: A web page that lists publication abstracts (some cut off with an ellipsis), not a paper. The text layer has no page breaks, so it counts as one page. The 'Content' index at the end repeats the titles.
papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc resource-library page that lists abstracts of publications, conference papers, a patent and theses on nonlinear photonics, mostly by the Huang and Kumar groups.

assertions.value: The authors report the first quantum frequency conversion temporal mode sorting system in a four-dimensional Hilbert space, with a conversion efficiency and mode separability as high as 92% and 0.84, respectively.
assertions.anchor: First listed entry, abstract snippet (Optica 3, 1300), page 1
quotes: We demonstrate the first QFC temporal mode sorting system in a four-dimensional Hilbert space, achieving a conversion efficiency and mode separability as high as 92% and 0.84, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract snippet on a vendor page; the evidence is in the cited paper, not in this page.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives no method or error bar for these figures.

assertions.value: The authors report sum-frequency generation between a telecom wavelength and the Rb D2 line in a nonlinear whispering gallery mode resonator, and state that the process saturates at sub-mW pump peak power, at least two orders of magnitude lower than in existing waveguide-based devices.
assertions.anchor: Second listed entry, abstract (New J. Phys. 16, 053025), page 1
quotes: the process saturates already at sub-mW pump peak power, at least two orders of magnitude lower than in existing waveguide-based devices
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract-level claim on a vendor page; no data shown here.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental all-optical interaction-free switch that uses the quantum Zeno effect, with a high contrast of 35∶ 1.
assertions.anchor: Third listed entry, abstract (Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 240403), page 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract-level empirical result on a vendor page.

assertions.value: The authors propose that a GaAs microdisk of 2.5-μm thickness and 10μm radius, with an intrinsic Q of ∼10^8 and a fiber-cavity-coupling Q of ∼10^4, can achieve low-loss (≲1%) switching for gigahertz-rate O-band quantum signals.
assertions.anchor: Fourth listed entry, abstract (Opt. Lett. 35, 2376), page 1
quotes: a 2.5-μm-thick, 10μm radius GaAs microdisk with an intrinsic Q of ∼10^8 and a fiber-cavity-coupling Q of ∼10^4 can achieve low-loss (≲1%) switching
assertions.certainty_reason: A design proposal stated in an abstract; not shown here.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a proposal (the abstract says 'We propose'), not a measured device.

assertions.value: The authors estimate that, with an on-chip toroidal microcavity immersed in rubidium vapor, high-fidelity entangled photons can be produced on-demand at MHz rates or higher.
assertions.anchor: Eighth listed entry, abstract (Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 030502), page 1
quotes: we estimate that high-fidelity entangled photons can be produced on-demand at MHz rates or higher
assertions.certainty_reason: An estimate stated in an abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says 'estimate', so this is a projection, not a measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report wideband optical parametric amplification over 14 THz covering telecom S, C, and L bands, with an observed maximum parametric gain of 38.3 dB, in a periodically poled LiNbO_3 waveguide.
assertions.anchor: Eleventh listed entry, abstract (Opt. Lett. 43, 2965), page 1
quotes: We report a wideband optical parametric amplification (OPA) over 14 THz covering telecom S, C, and L bands with observed maximum parametric gain of 38.3 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract-level empirical result on a vendor page.

assertions.value: The authors present a two-input, two-output, single-photon switch prototype that they state can achieve an insertion loss below 0.6 dB and a switching speed above 5 GHz.
assertions.anchor: Fourteenth listed entry, abstract (Rambo et al.), page 1
quotes: capable of achieving insertion loss <; 0.6 dB and switching speed > 5 GHz
assertions.certainty_reason: A two-sentence conference abstract; no data shown here.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says 'capable of achieving', which does not say these two figures were reached together.

assertions.value: The authors report photon-pair generation through spontaneous four-wave mixing in naturally occurring fluorescent proteins, with a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of about 145 in green fluorescent proteins.
assertions.anchor: Eighteenth listed entry, abstract (Sci. Rep., srep24344), page 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract-level empirical result on a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: A conference abstract on the same page gives a maximum ratio of about 70 for the same protein; the figures come from different papers.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental programmable parametric mode sorter of high-dimensional signals in a spatiotemporal Hilbert space, and state that optimizing pump temporal profiles gives more than 12-dB extinction.
assertions.anchor: Nineteenth listed entry, abstract (Phys. Rev. Applied 19, 044070), page 1
quotes: Optimizing pump temporal profiles allows us to achieve more than 12-dB extinction
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract-level empirical result on a vendor page; the abstract is cut off.
assertions.reader_inference: The sentence is cut off after 'mutually unbiased basis (MUB) sets of', so the full scope of the figure is not on this page.

assertions.value: The authors report a coincidence-to-accidental rate value of 1632.6, which they call a record high, in a heterogeneous design of hydrogenated amorphous silicon and silicon nitride waveguides, with a photon pair generation rate of 1.94 MHz.
quotes: A record high coincidence- to- accidental rate value of 1632.6 ( 260.4) is achieved in this heterogeneous design with a photon pair generation rate of 1.94 MHz.
assertions.certainty_reason: A preprint abstract on a vendor page; 'record' is the authors' own word.
assertions.reader_inference: The page does not say what the record is measured against.

assertions.value: The page shows abstract snippets only, and some end in an ellipsis; the entry on temporal mode sorting breaks off at the words 'including ...'.
quotes: A 20-GHz pulse train is projected onto 6 different TMs, including ...
assertions.certainty_reason: A reader observation about the text of this page.
assertions.reader_inference: Any figure taken from this page may miss conditions that the full paper states.
